title: Validate board provision metadata before raising the epoch floor
description: Security/robustness review finding discovered from the closed epoch-floor task. effective_epoch_floor in python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:201-205 blindly returns max(firmware_build_epoch, board_provision_epoch) for every non-None value. It validates neither types/ranges nor the provision value presence, authentication/integrity, nonzero status, relation to build epoch, deterministic maximum lead, or recoverability. A corrupted or malicious far-future provision epoch can therefore make all legitimate time samples fail indefinitely. This contradicts docs/firmware-time-provider.md:11-64, especially its explicit invalid-metadata diagnostics and recovery requirements; test/vectors/packets-timing.json:198-205 does not exercise validity metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Model board provision epoch as validated metadata including presence, parse/range result, authentication or integrity result, and configured deterministic lead bound. Ignore missing, zero, malformed, unauthenticated, earlier-than-build, overflow/out-of-range, and beyond-lead values; retain the firmware build epoch and expose a specific rejection diagnostic. Support authenticated replacement or clearing so a poisoned value cannot permanently lock out time. Validate firmware build metadata and integer bounds rather than relying on max coercion. Add the full docs/firmware-time-provider.md:152-166 matrix to Python tests and canonical vectors, including recovery and a legitimate stricter provision floor. Ensure consumers use only the validated effective floor; run focused tests and three code-review passes per modified source module.
notes: Post-fix correctness review: provision metadata only checks board_identity is non-None and minimum_record_version defaults to 0. Require the expected device identity/settings digest and a persistent rollback/version floor with no permissive production default; add identity-mismatch diagnostics/vectors and authenticated replace/clear recovery.
